# Information Security Risk Assessment, Continuous Monitoring, and Security Authorization Standard

## 1. Purpose and Scope

This standard establishes the requirements for risk assessment, security categorization, assessment and authorization, and continuous monitoring of information systems at Acme Health. This standard applies to all information systems that process, store, or transmit electronic protected health information and other organizational information assets.

## 2. Policy Framework

### 2.1 Risk Assessment Policy

Acme Health must develop, document, and disseminate a risk assessment policy that addresses purpose, scope, roles, responsibilities, management commitment, coordination among organizational entities, and compliance, and that is consistent with applicable laws, executive orders, directives, regulations, policies, standards, and guidelines. [NIST 800-53 RA-1 Low, Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE RA-1 AE Mandatory]

Acme Health must develop, document, and disseminate procedures to facilitate the implementation of the risk assessment policy and the associated risk assessment controls. [NIST 800-53 RA-1 Low, Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE RA-1 AE Mandatory]

Acme Health must designate an [Assignment: organization-defined official] to manage the development, documentation, and dissemination of the risk assessment policy and procedures. [NIST 800-53 RA-1 Low, Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE RA-1 AE Mandatory]

Acme Health must review and update the risk assessment policy [Assignment: organization-defined frequency] and following [Assignment: organization-defined events], and review and update the risk assessment procedures [Assignment: organization-defined frequency] and following [Assignment: organization-defined events]. [NIST 800-53 RA-1 Low, Moderate, High]

Acme Health must review and update the risk assessment policy at least every one (1) year and following organization-defined events, and review and update the risk assessment procedures at least every one (1) year and following organization-defined events. [ARC-AMPE RA-1 AE Mandatory]

### 2.2 Assessment, Authorization, and Monitoring Policy

Acme Health must develop, document, and disseminate an assessment, authorization, and monitoring policy that addresses purpose, scope, roles, responsibilities, management commitment, coordination among organizational entities, and compliance, and that is consistent with applicable laws, executive orders, directives, regulations, policies, standards, and guidelines. [NIST 800-53 CA-1 Low, Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE CA-1 AE Mandatory]

Acme Health must develop, document, and disseminate procedures to facilitate the implementation of the assessment, authorization, and monitoring policy and the associated assessment, authorization, and monitoring controls. [NIST 800-53 CA-1 Low, Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE CA-1 AE Mandatory]

Acme Health must designate an [Assignment: organization-defined official] to manage the development, documentation, and dissemination of the assessment, authorization, and monitoring policy and procedures. [NIST 800-53 CA-1 Low, Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE CA-1 AE Mandatory]

Acme Health must review and update the assessment, authorization, and monitoring policy [Assignment: organization-defined frequency] and following [Assignment: organization-defined events], and review and update the assessment, authorization, and monitoring procedures [Assignment: organization-defined frequency] and following [Assignment: organization-defined events]. [NIST 800-53 CA-1 Low, Moderate, High]

Acme Health must review and update the assessment, authorization, and monitoring policy at least every one (1) year and following organization-defined events, and review and update the assessment, authorization, and monitoring procedures at least every one (1) year and following organization-defined events. [ARC-AMPE CA-1 AE Mandatory]

### 2.3 HIPAA Security Policies and Procedures

Acme Health must implement reasonable and appropriate policies and procedures to comply with the standards, implementation specifications, or other requirements of this subpart, taking into account those factors specified in § 164.306(b)(2)(i), (ii), (iii), and (iv). [HIPAA Security Rule 164.316(a)]

Acme Health must implement policies and procedures to prevent, detect, contain, and correct security violations. [HIPAA Security Rule 164.308(a)(1)(i)]

## 3. Documentation Requirements

### 3.1 Maintenance of Documentation

Acme Health must maintain the policies and procedures implemented to comply with this subpart in written (which may be electronic) form, and maintain a written (which may be electronic) record of any action, activity, or assessment required by this subpart to be documented. [HIPAA Security Rule 164.316(b)(1)]

### 3.2 Retention

Acme Health must retain the documentation required by paragraph (b)(1) for 6 years from the date of its creation or the date when it last was in effect, whichever is later. [HIPAA Security Rule 164.316(b)(2)(i)]

### 3.3 Availability and Updates

Acme Health must make documentation available to those persons responsible for implementing the procedures to which the documentation pertains. [HIPAA Security Rule 164.316(b)(2)(ii)]

Acme Health must review documentation periodically, and update as needed, in response to environmental or operational changes affecting the security of the electronic protected health information. [HIPAA Security Rule 164.316(b)(2)(iii)]

## 4. Security Categorization

Acme Health must categorize the system and information it processes, stores, and transmits. [NIST 800-53 RA-2 Low, Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE RA-2 AE Mandatory]

Acme Health must document the security categorization results, including supporting rationale, in the security plan for the system. [NIST 800-53 RA-2 Low, Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE RA-2 AE Mandatory]

Acme Health must verify that the authorizing official or authorizing official designated representative reviews and approves the security categorization decision. [NIST 800-53 RA-2 Low, Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE RA-2 AE Mandatory]

## 5. Risk Assessment

### 5.1 Risk Assessment Performance

Acme Health must conduct a risk assessment, including: (1) identifying threats to and vulnerabilities in the system; (2) determining the likelihood and magnitude of harm from unauthorized access, use, disclosure, disruption, modification, or destruction of the system, the information it processes, stores, or transmits, and any related information; and (3) determining the likelihood and impact of adverse effects on individuals arising from the processing of personally identifiable information. [NIST 800-53 RA-3 Low, Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE RA-3 AE Mandatory]

Acme Health must conduct an accurate and thorough assessment of the potential risks and vulnerabilities to the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of electronic protected health information held by the covered entity or business associate. [HIPAA Security Rule 164.308(a)(1)(ii)(A)]

Acme Health must integrate risk assessment results and risk management decisions from the organization and mission or business process perspectives with system-level risk assessments. [NIST 800-53 RA-3 Low, Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE RA-3 AE Mandatory]

### 5.2 Risk Assessment Documentation

Acme Health must document risk assessment results in [Selection: security and privacy plans; risk assessment report; [Assignment: organization-defined document]]. [NIST 800-53 RA-3 Low, Moderate, High]

Acme Health must document risk assessment results in security and privacy plans, risk assessment report, and any additional organization-defined documents. [ARC-AMPE RA-3 AE Mandatory]

### 5.3 Risk Assessment Review and Updates

Acme Health must review risk assessment results [Assignment: organization-defined frequency]. [NIST 800-53 RA-3 Low, Moderate, High]

Acme Health must review risk assessment results at least every one (1) year or when a significant change occurs. [ARC-AMPE RA-3 AE Mandatory]

Acme Health must disseminate risk assessment results to [Assignment: organization-defined personnel or roles]. [NIST 800-53 RA-3 Low, Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE RA-3 AE Mandatory]

Acme Health must update the risk assessment [Assignment: organization-defined frequency] or when there are significant changes to the system, its environment of operation, or other conditions that may impact the security or privacy state of the system. [NIST 800-53 RA-3 Low, Moderate, High]

Acme Health must update the risk assessment at least every three (3) years at a minimum or when there are significant changes to the system, its environment of operation, or other conditions that may impact the security or privacy state of the system. [ARC-AMPE RA-3 AE Mandatory]

### 5.4 All-Source Intelligence

Acme Health must use all-source intelligence to assist in the analysis of risk. [NIST 800-53 RA-3(2) | ARC-AMPE RA-3(2) AE Mandatory]

Acme Health must use all-source intelligence consisting of information derived from all available sources, including publicly available or open-source information, to inform engineering, acquisition, and risk management decisions and to analyze the risk of vulnerabilities (both intentional and unintentional) from development, manufacturing, and delivery processes, people, and the environment. [ARC-AMPE RA-3(2) AE Mandatory]

## 6. Risk Management

### 6.1 Risk Reduction

Acme Health must implement security measures sufficient to reduce risks and vulnerabilities to a reasonable and appropriate level to comply with § 164.306(a). [HIPAA Security Rule 164.308(a)(1)(ii)(B)]

### 6.2 Response to Findings

Acme Health must respond to findings from security and privacy assessments, monitoring, and audits in accordance with organizational risk tolerance. [NIST 800-53 RA-7 Low, Moderate, High | FedRAMP RA-7 | ARC-AMPE RA-7 AE Mandatory]

Acme Health must follow the FedRAMP Vulnerability Detection and Response and Vulnerability Evaluation and Reporting rules when responding to findings. [FedRAMP RA-7]

## 7. Criticality Analysis

Acme Health must identify critical system components and functions by performing a criticality analysis for [Assignment: organization-defined systems, system components, or system services] at [Assignment: organization-defined decision points in the system development life cycle]. [NIST 800-53 RA-9 Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE RA-9 AE Mandatory]

All system components within the CMS Authority to Connect (ATC) / Request to Connect (RTC) boundary are considered critical, and all system components within the CMS State AE Authority to Connect (ATC) or the other ARC-AMPE User's Request to Connect (RTC) boundary are considered critical. [ARC-AMPE RA-9 AE Mandatory]

## 8. Contingency Planning

### 8.1 Emergency Response

Acme Health must establish (and implement as needed) policies and procedures for responding to an emergency or other occurrence (for example, fire, vandalism, system failure, and natural disaster) that damages systems that contain electronic protected health information. [HIPAA Security Rule 164.308(a)(7)(i)]

### 8.2 Data Backup and Recovery

Acme Health must establish and implement procedures to create and maintain retrievable exact copies of electronic protected health information. [HIPAA Security Rule 164.308(a)(7)(ii)(A)]

Acme Health must establish (and implement as needed) procedures to restore any loss of data. [HIPAA Security Rule 164.308(a)(7)(ii)(B)]

### 8.3 Emergency Mode Operations

Acme Health must establish (and implement as needed) procedures to enable continuation of critical business processes for protection of the security of electronic protected health information while operating in emergency mode. [HIPAA Security Rule 164.308(a)(7)(ii)(C)]

### 8.4 Testing and Revision

Acme Health must implement procedures for periodic testing and revision of contingency plans. [HIPAA Security Rule 164.308(a)(7)(ii)(D)]

### 8.5 Applications and Data Criticality Assessment

Acme Health must assess the relative criticality of specific applications and data in support of other contingency plan components. [HIPAA Security Rule 164.308(a)(7)(ii)(E)]

## 9. Security Assessment and Authorization

### 9.1 Assessment Planning

Acme Health must select the appropriate assessor or assessment team for the type of assessment to be conducted. [NIST 800-53 CA-2 Low, Moderate, High | FedRAMP CA-2 | ARC-AMPE CA-2 AE Mandatory]

Acme Health must develop a control assessment plan that describes the scope of the assessment including: (1) controls and control enhancements under assessment; (2) assessment procedures to be used to determine control effectiveness; and (3) assessment environment, assessment team, and assessment roles and responsibilities. [NIST 800-53 CA-2 Low, Moderate, High | FedRAMP CA-2 | ARC-AMPE CA-2 AE Mandatory]

Acme Health must ensure the control assessment plan is reviewed and approved by the authorizing official or designated representative prior to conducting the assessment. [NIST 800-53 CA-2 Low, Moderate, High | FedRAMP CA-2 | ARC-AMPE CA-2 AE Mandatory]

### 9.2 Security Control Assessment

Acme Health must assess the controls in the system and its environment of operation [Assignment: organization-defined assessment frequency] to determine the extent to which the controls are implemented correctly, operating as intended, and producing the desired outcome with respect to meeting established security and privacy requirements. [NIST 800-53 CA-2 Low, Moderate, High | FedRAMP CA-2]

Acme Health must assess the controls in the system and its environment of operation as specified in the supplemental control requirements & guidance to determine the extent to which the controls are implemented correctly, operating as intended, and producing the desired outcome with respect to meeting established security and privacy requirements. [ARC-AMPE CA-2 AE Mandatory]

A complete independent assessment of all security and privacy controls must be conducted over a three (3) year period by: (a) undergoing a full controls assessment at the end of the ATC lifespan and delivering the complete and final ATC package no less than ninety (90) days prior to the ATC's expiration; or (b) undergoing independent assessments of the annually required controls designated by CMS for years one (1), two (2), and three (3) such that all ARC-AMPE controls are assessed within the three (3) year period and delivering the complete and final ATC package no less than ninety (90) days prior to expiration; or (c) by responding to CMS guidance on what, if any, documents or independent testing must be completed for each significant system change based on CMS' determination of any impact to the ATC. [ARC-AMPE CA-2 AE Mandatory]

Acme Health must produce a control assessment report that documents the results of the assessment. [NIST 800-53 CA-2 Low, Moderate, High | FedRAMP CA-2 | ARC-AMPE CA-2 AE Mandatory]

### 9.3 Assessment Results Distribution

Acme Health must provide the results of the control assessment to [Assignment: organization-defined individuals or roles]. [NIST 800-53 CA-2 Low, Moderate, High]

Acme Health must provide the results of the control assessment to individuals or roles to include FedRAMP and agency customers. [FedRAMP CA-2]

Acme Health must provide the results of the control assessment to the Business Owner responsible for the system and personnel responsible for reviewing the assessment documentation, and updating security and privacy documentation where necessary to reflect any changes to the system within thirty (30) days after its completion in writing. [ARC-AMPE CA-2 AE Mandatory]

### 9.4 Independent Assessors

Acme Health must employ independent assessors or assessment teams to conduct control assessments. [NIST 800-53 CA-2(1) Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE CA-2(1) AE Mandatory]

Acme Health must employ independent assessors or assessment teams approved by the organization's Chief Information Security Officer (CISO) or equivalent to conduct control assessments. [ARC-AMPE CA-2(1) AE Mandatory]

### 9.5 Leveraging External Assessments

Acme Health must leverage the results of control assessments performed by [Assignment: organization-defined external organization(s)] on [Assignment: organization-defined system] when the assessment meets [Assignment: organization-defined requirements]. [NIST 800-53 CA-2(3) | FedRAMP CA-2(3)]

Acme Health must leverage the results of control assessments performed by any FedRAMP Recognized independent assessment service when the assessment meets organization-defined requirements. [FedRAMP CA-2(3)]

### 9.6 Periodic Technical and Nontechnical Evaluation

Acme Health must perform a periodic technical and nontechnical evaluation, based initially upon the standards implemented under this rule and, subsequently, in response to environmental or operational changes affecting the security of electronic protected health information, that establishes the extent to which a covered entity's or business associate's security policies and procedures meet the requirements of this subpart. [HIPAA Security Rule 164.308(a)(8)]

## 10. Plan of Action and Milestones

Acme Health must develop a plan of action and milestones for the system to document the planned remediation actions of the organization to correct weaknesses or deficiencies noted during the assessment of the controls and to reduce or eliminate known vulnerabilities in the system. [NIST 800-53 CA-5 Low, Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE CA-5 AE Mandatory]

Acme Health must update existing plan of action and milestones [Assignment: organization-defined frequency] based on the findings from control assessments, independent audits or reviews, and continuous monitoring activities. [NIST 800-53 CA-5 Low, Moderate, High]

Acme Health must update existing plan of action and milestones in accordance with the frequency documented in the organization's Information Security Continuous Monitoring (ISCM) strategy based on the findings from control assessments, independent audits or reviews, and continuous monitoring activities. [ARC-AMPE CA-5 AE Mandatory]

Acme Health must deliver to CMS a fully updated and accurate POA&M quarterly on 31 January, 30 April, 31 July, and 31 October. [ARC-AMPE CA-5 AE Mandatory]

## 11. Security Authorization

### 11.1 Authorizing Official

Acme Health must assign a senior official as the authorizing official for the system. [NIST 800-53 CA-6 Low, Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE CA-6 AE Mandatory]

Acme Health must assign a senior official as the authorizing official for common controls available for inheritance by organizational systems. [NIST 800-53 CA-6 Low, Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE CA-6 AE Mandatory]

### 11.2 Authorization Requirements

Acme Health must ensure that the authorizing official for the system, before commencing operations: (1) accepts the use of common controls inherited by the system; and (2) authorizes the system to operate. [NIST 800-53 CA-6 Low, Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE CA-6 AE Mandatory]

Acme Health must ensure that the authorizing official for common controls authorizes the use of those controls for inheritance by organizational systems. [NIST 800-53 CA-6 Low, Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE CA-6 AE Mandatory]

### 11.3 Authorization Updates

Acme Health must update the authorizations [Assignment: organization-defined frequency]. [NIST 800-53 CA-6 Low, Moderate, High]

Acme Health must update the authorizations at least every three (3) years for all entities (except Direct Enrollment Technology Providers which must update their authorization at least every one (1) year), when significant security breaches occur, whenever there is a significant change to the system or to the environment in which the system operates, or prior to expiration of a current authorization. [ARC-AMPE CA-6 AE Mandatory]

## 12. Continuous Monitoring

### 12.1 Continuous Monitoring Strategy

Acme Health must develop a system-level continuous monitoring strategy and implement continuous monitoring in accordance with the organization-level continuous monitoring strategy that establishes system-level metrics to be monitored. [NIST 800-53 CA-7 Low, Moderate, High | FedRAMP CA-7]

Acme Health must develop a system-level continuous monitoring strategy and implement continuous monitoring in accordance with the organization-level continuous monitoring strategy that establishes system-level metrics to be monitored based on the organization security and privacy goals and in accordance with organization's Information Security Continuous Monitoring (ISCM) strategy. [ARC-AMPE CA-7 AE Mandatory]

### 12.2 Monitoring Frequencies

Acme Health must establish [Assignment: organization-defined frequencies] for monitoring and [Assignment: organization-defined frequencies] for assessment of control effectiveness. [NIST 800-53 CA-7 Low, Moderate, High | FedRAMP CA-7]

Acme Health must establish at least once a month scans for operating system, databases, and web applications for monitoring and no less than at least every one (1) year for assessment of control effectiveness. [ARC-AMPE CA-7 AE Mandatory]

### 12.3 Continuous Monitoring Activities

Acme Health must perform ongoing control assessments in accordance with the continuous monitoring strategy. [NIST 800-53 CA-7 Low, Moderate, High | FedRAMP CA-7 | ARC-AMPE CA-7 AE Mandatory]

Acme Health must perform ongoing monitoring of system and organization-defined metrics in accordance with the continuous monitoring strategy. [NIST 800-53 CA-7 Low, Moderate, High | FedRAMP CA-7 | ARC-AMPE CA-7 AE Mandatory]

Acme Health must perform correlation and analysis of information generated by control assessments and monitoring. [NIST 800-53 CA-7 Low, Moderate, High | FedRAMP CA-7 | ARC-AMPE CA-7 AE Mandatory]

Acme Health must perform response actions to address results of the analysis of control assessment and monitoring information. [NIST 800-53 CA-7 Low, Moderate, High | FedRAMP CA-7 | ARC-AMPE CA-7 AE Mandatory]

### 12.4 Status Reporting

Acme Health must report the security and privacy status of the system to [Assignment: organization-defined personnel or roles] [Assignment: organization-defined frequency]. [NIST 800-53 CA-7 Low, Moderate, High]

Acme Health must report the security and privacy status of the system to organization-defined personnel or roles at least every thirty (30) days (monthly). [ARC-AMPE CA-7 AE Mandatory]

### 12.5 FedRAMP Continuous Monitoring

Acme Health must follow the FedRAMP Continuous Collaborative Monitoring, Significant Change Notification, Vulnerability Detection and Response, and Vulnerability Evaluation and Reporting rules when implementing continuous monitoring. [FedRAMP CA-7]

### 12.6 Independent Monitoring

Acme Health must employ independent assessors or assessment teams to monitor the controls in the system on an ongoing basis. [NIST 800-53 CA-7(1) Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE CA-7(1) AE Mandatory]

### 12.7 Risk Monitoring

Acme Health must ensure risk monitoring is an integral part of the continuous monitoring strategy that includes: (a) effectiveness monitoring; (b) compliance monitoring; and (c) change monitoring. [NIST 800-53 CA-7(4) Low, Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE CA-7(4) AE Mandatory]

Acme Health must update the continuous monitoring strategy to document processes and guidance for what is considered effectiveness monitoring, compliance monitoring, and change monitoring as part of a holistic risk monitoring strategy. [ARC-AMPE CA-7(4) AE Mandatory]

## 13. Penetration Testing

### 13.1 Penetration Testing Performance

Acme Health must conduct penetration testing [Assignment: organization-defined frequency] on [Assignment: organization-defined system(s) or system components]. [NIST 800-53 CA-8 High | FedRAMP CA-8]

Acme Health must conduct penetration testing at least every one (1) year on organization-defined systems or system components as agreed with the penetration testers in the Rules of Engagement. [ARC-AMPE CA-8 AE Mandatory]

Penetration testing is part of vulnerability detection and is subject to the Vulnerability Detection and Response rules. [FedRAMP CA-8]

### 13.2 Independent Penetration Testing

Acme Health must employ an independent penetration testing agent or team to perform penetration testing on the system or system components. [NIST 800-53 CA-8(1) High | ARC-AMPE CA-8(1) AE Mandatory]

Acme Health must employ an independent penetration testing agent or team approved by the organization's Chief Information Security Officer (CISO) or equivalent to perform penetration testing on the system or system components. [ARC-AMPE CA-8(1) AE Mandatory]

## 14. Information System Activity Review

Acme Health must implement procedures to regularly review records of information system activity, such as audit logs, access reports, and security incident tracking reports. [HIPAA Security Rule 164.308(a)(1)(ii)(D)]

## 15. Roles and Responsibilities

### 15.1 Security Official

Acme Health must identify the security official who is responsible for the development and implementation of the policies and procedures required by this subpart for the covered entity or business associate. [HIPAA Security Rule 164.308(a)(2)]

## 16. Sanctions

Acme Health must apply appropriate sanctions against workforce members who fail to comply with the security policies and procedures of the covered entity or business associate. [HIPAA Security Rule 164.308(a)(1)(ii)(C)]

---

**Document Control**

This standard must be reviewed and updated in accordance with the frequencies specified in Section 2 and in response to environmental or operational changes affecting the security of information systems and electronic protected health information.
